content.title: About
content.content: Turnover is a ready‑to‑eat fruit pastry made of flaky dough filled with a sweet fruit mixture. It is popular as a quick snack or dessert and is often sold frozen for later heating.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turnovers originated in Europe in the 19th century as a street‑food treat.
The dough is typically made from flour, butter, eggs, and a small amount of sugar, giving it a crisp texture.
Fillings can include apples, cherries, peaches, apricots, or a blend of several fruits.
Turnovers are often served warm to release the aroma of the fruit and buttery pastry.
In some countries they are called “fruit hand pie” or simply “fruit turnover.”

items.title: Fruit source
items.content: The fruit filling provides vitamins C and A as well as dietary fiber that supports digestion.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Turnovers contain carbohydrates that quickly replenish energy stores.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Fruits in the filling are rich in antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The sweet fruit filling can raise blood sugar levels, so people with diabetes should limit consumption.

items.title: Possible trans fats
items.content: If the dough is made with margarine or partially hydrogenated oils, the product may contain trans fats, which are detrimental to heart health.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The dough usually contains wheat flour, making it unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the turnover in an oven or microwave until the crust is golden, then serve warm. It can be eaten by hand or sliced and added to ice cream or yogurt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen turnovers in a freezer at –18 °C. After thawing, consume within 24 hours and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
